elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: SFJ is required to indemnify and hold harmless, but no operative duty to defend PB appears.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Sections 12.1.1 and the added SFJ IP Indemnity require SFJ to indemnify PB for specified Third Party Claims.

elements.element: Vendor's defense and indemnity protection must extend to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: PB's Affiliates are included among the PB Indemnified Parties for indemnification, but the required defense obligation is absent.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity must apply to third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The added clause covers any Claim by a Third Party, and Section 12.1.1 likewise applies to Claims by a Third Party.

elements.element: Vendor must cover claims alleging that the services infringe intellectual property.
elements.evidence: The added clause covers Third Party Claims alleging that services provided by SFJ under the Agreement infringe or misappropriate Intellectual Property.

elements.element: Vendor must cover claims alleging that the deliverables infringe intellectual property.
elements.evidence: The added clause expressly covers Third Party Claims alleging that deliverables provided by SFJ infringe or misappropriate Intellectual Property.

elements.element: Vendor must cover third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: No SFJ indemnity trigger addresses SFJ's breach or violation of applicable law.

elements.element: Vendor must cover third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No indemnity trigger addresses a data or security breach caused by SFJ.

elements.element: Vendor must cover third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Section 12.1.1(a) covers Third Party Claims arising from SFJ's gross negligence in performing its obligations.

elements.element: Vendor must cover third-party claims arising from Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 12.1.1(a) covers Third Party Claims arising from SFJ's willful misconduct in performing its obligations.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require notice of a covered claim.
elements.evidence: The rendered language contains no claims-notice procedure.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must give the indemnifying party control of the defense and settlement.
elements.evidence: The rendered language does not allocate control of defense or settlement.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require reasonable cooperation from the indemnified party.
elements.evidence: The rendered language contains no cooperation obligation.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: PB's indemnity does not expressly identify PB-provided content as an indemnity trigger.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: PB's material breach of the Agreement and Protocol breaches are covered, but no indemnity trigger expressly covers PB's breach of law.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must be limited exclusively to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 12.1.2 imposes substantially broader PB indemnities, including for Products supplied by PB, contractual and Protocol breaches, IP infringement, subject injuries, Clinical Trials, and Commercialization.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party intellectual-property infringement claims concerning Vendor's services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: The added SFJ IP Indemnity covers PB Indemnified Parties for Third Party Claims alleging that SFJ's services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate Intellectual Property.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims arising from Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: The added clause excludes claims to the extent arising from modifications made by PB.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims arising from Customer combinations with items not supplied by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The added clause excludes claims arising from PB's combination of the services or deliverables with items not supplied by SFJ.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims arising from Vendor's compliance with Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: The added clause excludes claims arising from SFJ's compliance with specifications provided by PB.

elements.element: Vendor must have a remedy to procure Customer's continued right to use the infringing item.
elements.evidence: SFJ may procure for PB the right to continue using the infringing item.

elements.element: Vendor must have a remedy to modify the infringing item.
elements.evidence: The added clause permits SFJ to modify the item.

elements.element: Vendor must have a remedy to replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: The added clause permits SFJ to replace the item.

elements.element: Vendor must refund amounts paid for the infringing item if procurement, modification, and replacement are unavailable.
elements.evidence: If none of the preceding remedies is available on commercially reasonable terms, SFJ must refund the amounts paid for the item.

elements.element: Vendor's IP indemnity liability must be subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: The added clause states that SFJ's aggregate liability under the IP indemnity section will not exceed 3x the annual fees payable under the Agreement.

result.reason: The redline fully implements the fallback through an SFJ IP indemnity, the three stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and a 3x annual-fees cap. It does not satisfy the preferred position because it omits a defense duty, breach-of-law and Vendor-caused data-breach triggers, claims procedures, and the required limitation of PB's indemnity. The change is substantively minimal for the fallback and does not directly negate existing commercial terms, although drafting quality is reduced by the unnumbered paragraph's reference to “Section 12.1.3,” an undefined annual-fee measurement period, ambiguous references such as “it,” and defects retained in the surrounding clause.
